modv0.1.0

claimGuard a tree with more than one writer.

The mod notices files that changed while this session was idle, tells the model once, and refuses sweeping git commands while those files are dirty.

At the prompt of a terminal session:

/plugin install claim --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills
Other ways to install

  • From a shell:

    claude plugin install claim --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills

  • In the desktop app: click + next to the prompt box, then Plugins, Add marketplace with LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills, then Add plugin.

Read atomic-commits Source on GitHub

Commands

CommandWhat it does
/claimwhat claim knows about this working tree
/claim take <path>accept one foreign file as this session's work
/claim take allaccept every foreign file
/claim offswitch detection and the guard off for this session
/claim onswitch them back on

In use

While a foreign file is dirty, these commands are refused: git add -A (and --all, -u, .), git commit -a, a stash, git reset --hard, git checkout ., git restore . and git clean -f. The refusal names the foreign files. A command that names explicit paths passes, and so does everything else, and nothing is refused once no foreign file is dirty.

Only a person can take a file or switch the guard off or on, by typing /claim. The same command from a plugin, a schedule or a peer prints the report and changes nothing, and the mod registers no tool for the model.

How it behaves

  • The rule. This session changes the tree only while one of its own write-capable calls runs, subagents included. A dirty file whose size or modification time changed while none was running was changed by someone else, and is called foreign.
  • Telling the model. Once for each new set of foreign files, attached to the next tool result and marked [claim], with the paths given as data. You get a toast and a claim: N foreign status entry.
  • The guard. It reads the Bash tool's command, including compound commands, git -C and options before the subcommand, and environment prefixes. It does not see a sweeping command inside a script, an alias or a Makefile target, and it does not see shells other than the Bash tool.
  • Background commands. Detection pauses while a command this session moved to the background is running, because its writes cannot be told from another writer's. It resumes with a fresh baseline when a turn ends with none left, or at /claim on.
  • Taking a file. /claim take and a commit both take a file off the list. A taken file returns only if it changes again while the session is idle.
  • What it can get wrong. It can call a file foreign when a tool it does not know as a writer changed it between calls. It misses a foreign change that lands while one of this session's own write-capable calls is running. Above 300 dirty entries it compares status codes only, so a second change to an already-changed file is not seen.
  • Cost. Two read-only git status runs around each write-capable call, each with a 5 second limit.
  • Outside git. It does nothing, and /claim says so.
